effects: The exact `assets` amount of XSGD moves from the signer to the vault (safeTransferFrom in enter), spending the signer's XSGD allowance to the vault.
steakXSGD vault shares are minted to `onBehalf`. The number of shares is previewDeposit(assets), computed from the vault's exchange rate after accrueInterest.
formats.shown: Deposit <amount> XSGD for <onBehalf>, with fields for the XSGD amount, a 'Share ticker: steakXSGD' constant and the share recipient.

findings.title: deposit: the number of steakXSGD shares received is not shown; it depends on the vault rate.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` computed from storage. Case 0: the signer received 12602452034685256 steakXSGD, and the screen shows no share amount. The reader wrote 'the amount is not shown'.
findings.fix: None in calldata. Optionally add a note that shares are priced at the current vault rate.

findings.title: deposit: the 'Share ticker' raw constant field does not say these shares are what the signer receives.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {label:'Share ticker', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker'}. Case 0 screen: 'Share ticker: steakXSGD'.
findings.fix: Relabel it 'Receive shares' (value steakXSGD) or put it in the sentence: 'Deposit {assets} for steakXSGD shares to {onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The XSGD out amount and asset are correct. The steakXSGD shares received show recipient and ticker but no amount, which is set by the vault rate.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `assets` XSGD is sent from the vault to `receiver`.
steakXSGD shares are burned from `onBehalf`. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up from the vault rate, and has no maximum in calldata.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer spends onBehalf's share allowance by the burned shares.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly <assets> XSGD to <receiver>, with the Owner (onBehalf) shown as a field.

findings.title: withdraw: the steakXSGD shares burned are neither named nor counted; the count depends on the vault rate.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)` then `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 2: 2.373086675367780848 steakXSGD burned from the signer, and the screen names no shares at all. The reader was unsure how many shares are burned.
findings.fix: The amount cannot come from calldata. Relabel 'Owner' to 'Burn steakXSGD shares from' so the signer knows the asset that leaves.

cases.notes: The XSGD received (exact amount and recipient) is shown. The shares burned show only the owner address, with no asset name or amount.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `shares` steakXSGD are burned from `onBehalf`, spending the signer's share allowance from onBehalf if the signer is not onBehalf.
XSGD equal to previewRedeem(shares), rounded down from the vault rate, is sent from the vault to `receiver`. There is no minimum-out parameter.
formats.shown: Redeem <shares> steakXSGD to <receiver>, with the owner shown as a field. Nothing says which asset arrives or how much.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never says XSGD is received; the signer only sees shares and a recipient.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit(): `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. Case 3: the signer received 1.084106 XSGD. The fields are only 'Shares to redeem', 'To' and 'Owner'. The reader wrote 'Exact amount and identity of the token I get back; the screen doesn't say' and 'likely XSGD'. mint already uses an underlyingTicker constant field, so redeem can too.
findings.fix: Add a field {label:'Receive asset', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'} and say 'Redeem {shares} for XSGD to {receiver}' in interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: redeem: the XSGD amount received is set by the vault rate, and calldata has no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);` with no min-assets parameter. Case 3: 1084106 XSGD received, and no amount or bound is shown.
findings.fix: None in calldata. A router with slippage protection would be needed for a bound.

cases.notes: The shares burned are shown exactly. The XSGD received has neither asset nor amount on screen; the reader guessed the asset.

effects: XSGD equal to previewMint(shares), rounded up from the vault rate, moves from the signer to the vault, spending the signer's XSGD allowance. No maximum is in calldata.
formats.shown: Mint <shares> steakXSGD for <onBehalf>, with a 'Deposit asset: XSGD' constant field and no XSGD amount.

findings.title: mint: the XSGD amount pulled from the signer is not shown and has no maximum in calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint(): `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);` then `safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. Case 1: the signer paid 1.003734 XSGD, and the screen shows only 'Deposit asset: XSGD'. The reader wrote 'The exact XSGD amount you pay is not shown.'
findings.fix: None in calldata. Add a label note that the XSGD cost is set by the vault rate, limited only by the signer's XSGD allowance.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' and its sentence never say the signer pays XSGD.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint intent 'Mint', interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. Case 1: 'Mint 0.999999999 steakXSGD for 0x...dEaD', while 1.003734 XSGD leaves the signer.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Deposit XSGD' and interpolatedIntent 'Deposit XSGD to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The XSGD out is named but has no amount or bound. The shares went to 0xdead, which is not the signer, and that is shown correctly.
